name: SQL (SQLite)
conventions: SQL challenges run on SQLite 3.46 (window functions, CTEs incl. recursive, UPSERT, RETURNING, STRICT tables, JSON functions). The user writes ONE query in starter/solution.sql (solution/solution.sql and every bugs/<name>/solution.sql likewise). README.md documents the schema as a code block. tests/schema.sql creates the tables; the Python unittest suite (stdlib only) builds a fresh in-memory database per test, inserts that test's rows, runs the query read from ../$TARGET/solution.sql and compares fetchall() to the expected rows (as lists, order-sensitive when the README specifies ORDER BY). Name tests after the rule they check: `bugs[].expect` matches the failing test's name. Golden tables are datasets in tests/cases.json (fixed seed, every edge case class: NULLs, duplicates, ties, empty tables, rows that should be excluded) with expected rows computed by running the REFERENCE query in the sandbox. Typical bug variants: INNER vs LEFT JOIN, a filter in WHERE that turns a LEFT JOIN into an INNER one, COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col), NULL comparisons with = instead of IS, missing tie-breakers in ORDER BY, window frames (ROWS vs RANGE).

areas.name: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY with tie-breakers
GROUP BY, HAVING and aggregate functions
NULL semantics (IS NULL, COALESCE, three-valued logic)
Window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, running totals, LAG/LEAD)
CTEs, including recursive (hierarchies, gaps and islands)
Indexes and query plans (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN)

levelNotes.1: Single-table filters/sorts or one join; small schemas (2 tables).
levelNotes.3: Window functions or CTEs; 3+ tables; tricky NULLs and ties.
levelNotes.5: Performance: require an index or rewrite; tests can assert EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN uses an index.
